newsitem.title: USA: Mrs. Clinton disagrees with husband on golf.
newsitem.headline: Mrs. Clinton disagrees with husband on golf.

text.p: First lady Hillary Rodham Clinton on Monday admitted to having some disagreements with her husband, particularly when it comes to watching movies and sports -- and definitely when it comes to playing golf.

Asked to describe areas where she and President Bill Clinton disagree, she said that she had tried "to become a golfer" to share the pasttime her husband loves, but it was doomed by a disasterous date she had had as a teenager.

"I don't like violent movies," Mrs. Clinton said in an interview from Washington with Michael Jackson, a host with Los Angeles radio station KABC. "He finds them relaxing. I think that's kind of a male thing."
"I like sports, but to be able to watch it eight, 12, 16 hours a day as he would if he had the time ... I think there are some other things we could do together," she said.
She said she has "taken lessons twice to become a golfer," but admitted "I have just never gotten there. I try, I try."
She blamed it on a date she had when she was 14 with "an older boy about 18." Her mother would not let the boy take her daughter out at night so as a compromise their date was at a golf course.
"I am as blind as a bat," said Clinton, who often wears contact lenses.

"So I didn't wear my glasses, because of course this was such an important date in my life. I went around not being able to see a thing and kept swinging at anything light. There I was exploding mushrooms all over this golf course," she said, laughing.
"I have never gotten over it," she added, explaining her inability to become passionate about golf. "I think I'm just blocked."
